title: Lower Burgundy
capsule: Lower Burgundy took shape in the Rhone valley and Provence as Carolingian central authority collapsed in the later 9th century, crystallizing when the regional magnate Boso of Provence - brother-in-law of Emperor Charles the Fat and widower of a Carolingian princess - was elected king at the Synod of Mantaille in October 879, the first non-Carolingian to claim a Frankish crown. Boso's kingship went largely unrecognized outside Provence and the lower Rhone, and after early losses to a Carolingian coalition he held only a shrunken realm until his death in 887. His son Louis the Blind, crowned in 890, inherited this Provencal-Burgundian kingdom, later adding the Italian crown before being blinded and deposed there in 905, after which his regent Hugh of Arles governed Lower Burgundy in his name.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The polity's territory is reconstructed from Carolingian diplomas and episcopal lists; precise frontiers, especially toward northern Burgundy and Italy, are disputed in the scholarship.
